Responsibility: the risk is produced by objectui's own approvals action bar, which labels a recall "Override Recall" and tells the admin it finalises the step and is recorded as an admin override (the server records neither), and frames a submitter-admin's own recall as an override; the platform path that covers it: none (the dialog is the only statement of the consequence); who reaches it: every admin who recalls a pending request, their own included.
Thread-read: none
The card had no comment at this claim. It was filed by this seat from objectui#13164's dev report (`6288370239`), and objectui#13164 has landed (`6288801287`).
Serial constraints cleared:
- No open objectui PR touches `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx` or `approvalOverride.ts`.
- Open objectui#13227 (another seat's objectui#13146) adds `settingsView.fieldErrorsToast*` to all ten packs, about 2,500 lines from `approvalsInbox`. Any key here stays in `approvalsInbox`, and the dev merges `main` before `pr_create` if objectui#13227 has landed.
- objectui#13151's PR #13226 (this seat, landing) holds `ObjectListViewInspector.tsx` and `metadata-admin/i18n.ts`.

Why `Clause-②: yes`: the claim cannot yet say whether the recall can be described with existing copy. A new `approvalsInbox.*` key would widen `@object-ui/i18n`'s exported `TranslationKeys` (precedent: objectui#13164). 「拿不准 ⇒ 按 `yes`」. The dev reports which it was.
